stem: A relation R on A = {1, 2, 3, 4} is defined by R = {(1,2), (2,1), (2,3), (3,2), (1,3), (3,1)}. Which of the following correctly describes the properties of R?

options.text: Symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
Reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
Transitive and symmetric but not reflexive

per_option_rationale.rationale: R is symmetric: every pair (a,b) has (b,a) in R. R is not reflexive: (1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4) are all absent. R is not transitive: (1,2) and (2,3) are in R but (1,3) actually IS in R; however (2,1) and (1,3) give (2,3) in R - still holds. Check (3,2) and (2,1): need (3,1) - yes in R. Check (2,1) and (1,2): need (2,2) - NOT in R. So R is not transitive.
R is not reflexive because (1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4) are absent from R.
R is not transitive: (2,1) and (1,2) are in R but (2,2) is not, violating transitivity.
R is not an equivalence relation because it fails both reflexive and transitive properties.

explanation: Reflexive check: (1,1) is not in R, so R is not reflexive. Symmetric check: for every (a,b) in R, (b,a) is also present - verified for all six pairs. Transitive check: (2,1) in R and (1,2) in R, but (2,2) is not in R, so R is not transitive. Therefore R is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.

explanation_sections.punchline: Symmetry holds because every pair has its reverse; transitivity fails at the (2,1),(1,2) combination which demands (2,2).
explanation_sections.approach: State each definition and test it against R systematically: (1) check if (a,a) is in R for every a - fails at element 1. (2) check if (a,b) in R implies (b,a) - passes for all six pairs. (3) check if any chain (a,b),(b,c) in R forces (a,c) - fails at a=2,b=1,c=2.
explanation_sections.lesson: To disprove transitivity, find a composable pair (a,b) and (b,c) where (a,c) is absent; the hardest case is a=c giving a self-loop requirement.
explanation_sections.timing: 70 s. The transitivity trap is missing the (2,1)+(1,2) -> (2,2) case because (1,3)+(3,1) -> (1,1) also fails but is less visible.
